hints: Focus on the word all. Think about what can squeeze through the tiny gaps in capillary walls to get from blood plasma into tissue fluid and then into lymph.

Remember that small dissolved substances like gases and glucose move freely, and that white blood cells and plasma proteins like antibodies are also able to leave the blood, unlike red blood cells and platelets.
walkthrough:
**Start with how the fluids are connected**

Think of blood, tissue fluid and lymph as one connected system. Tissue fluid is made when plasma is forced out of capillaries, and lymph is just drained tissue fluid. So anything small enough to leave the capillary will be in all three.

Key rule: small molecules and some cells and proteins can exit, large cells like red blood cells cannot.

**Check the small dissolved substances**

Carbon dioxide (1) is carried dissolved in plasma in all vessels, even arteries contain some. Glucose (2) is also dissolved in plasma everywhere to supply cells. Both are tiny, so they filter out easily into tissue fluid and then into lymph. So 1 and 2 are in all three fluids.

**Check the defence components**

White blood cells (3) can squeeze between endothelial cells by diapedesis to patrol tissues and lymph. Antibodies (4) are soluble plasma proteins made by lymphocytes, so they also leave capillaries in the tissue fluid and are carried away in lymph. So 3 and 4 are also in all three fluids.

**Put it together**

Since 1, 2, 3 and 4 are all found in every blood vessel plus lymph plus tissue fluid, the correct combination is 1, 2, 3 and 4.

options.A: Correct. Carbon dioxide, glucose, white blood cells and antibodies are all small or mobile enough to be in plasma everywhere and to pass into tissue fluid and lymph.
options.B: Misses out antibodies. Antibodies are soluble plasma proteins that do enter tissue fluid and lymph, so 4 should be included.
options.C: Misses out glucose. Glucose is dissolved in all blood plasma and filters into tissue fluid and lymph to supply cells, so 2 should be included.
options.D: Misses out carbon dioxide and white blood cells. Both are present in all vessels and can enter tissue fluid and lymph, so 1 and 3 should be included.
